subject: History

stem: Who was the governor general of India during Sepoy Mutiny?
solution: The Sepoy Mutiny (the Revolt of 1857) broke out in May 1857, when Lord Canning was Governor-General of India (1856-1858). He continued after the revolt as the first Viceroy of India under Crown rule. Lord Dalhousie (1848-1856) preceded him and his Doctrine of Lapse was a cause of the revolt, but he had already left India. Lord Hardinge (Henry Hardinge, 1844-1848) and Lord Lytton (1876-1880) held office well before and well after the revolt respectively. Matches option A.

subject: History
subtopic: Freedom Movement — INC, Gandhi and Independence
stem: Who was the leader of the Ghadar Party?
solution: The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 at San Francisco by Indian emigrants. Lala Har Dayal was its principal ideologue and general secretary, and is conventionally named as its leader (Sohan Singh Bhakna was the first president). Bhagat Singh belonged to the later Hindustan Socialist Republican Association, Tilak led the Extremists within the Congress, and V.D. Savarkar led Abhinav Bharat. Matches option B.

solution: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Calcutta Unitarian Committee was set up in 1821 by Raja Ram Mohan Roy along with William Adam and Dwarkanath Tagore, well before Keshab Chandra Sen's time. Statement 2 is correct: Keshab Chandra Sen proclaimed the Nava Vidhan (New Dispensation) in 1880 and established its Tabernacle of New Dispensation. Statement 3 is correct: he founded the Indian Reform Association in 1870 to carry out social reform work in education, temperance and women's uplift. So only 2 and 3. Matches option B.

stem: Which among the following events happened earliest?

solution: Dinabandhu Mitra wrote Neel Darpan, the play on indigo planter oppression, in 1858-59 and it was published in 1860. Satyendranath Tagore cleared the Indian Civil Service examination in 1863. Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875. Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote Anandamath in 1882. The earliest of the four is therefore Neel Darpan. Matches option B.

1. Responsible for starting the home rule movement
2. The founder of the Theosophical Society
3. The president of the Indian National Congress
Which of the statements given above is/ are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is correct: Annie Besant announced her Home Rule League in September 1916 and, with Tilak, drove the Home Rule Movement. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Theosophical Society was founded in New York in 1875 by Madame H.P. Blavatsky and Colonel H.S. Olcott; Besant only joined in 1889 and became its president in 1907. Statement 3 is correct: she presided over the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1917, the first woman to do so. So 1 and 3 only. Matches option C.

subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: The world's largest Ocean is shrinking due to
optA: The absence of deep ocean trenches at plate margins
optB: The faster addition of new crust than the occurrence subduction process
optC: The subduction is occurring faster than the addition of new crust.
optD: Increasing number of volcanic eruptions in the ring of fire.
solution: The world's largest ocean is the Pacific. New oceanic crust is generated along the East Pacific Rise, but the Pacific is almost completely ringed by convergent margins with deep trenches, the Ring of Fire, where the Pacific plate is being consumed by subduction. Because crust is destroyed at these trenches faster than it is created at the ridge, the Pacific basin is slowly contracting, whereas the Atlantic, having few subduction zones, is widening. Options A and B state the opposite of the facts and option D confuses the surface expression, volcanism, with the cause, subduction. Matches option C.

stem: During Indian freedom struggle, the National Social Conference was formed. What was the reason for its formation?
optA: Different social reform groups or organizations of Bengal region united to form a single body to discuss the issues of larger interest and to prepare appropriate petitions /representations

Consider the following statements about Hindu women's inheritance rights.
1. The Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005 gave Hindu women the right to be coparceners or joint legal heirs in the same way a male heir does.
2. The law applies to ancestral property and to intestate succession in personal property - where succession happens as per law and not through a will.
3. The law applied to everyone who is not a Muslim
Which of the following given above is/ are correct
solution: Statement 1 is correct: the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005 amended Section 6 so that a daughter becomes a coparcener in a Hindu Undivided Family by birth in her own right, in the same manner as a son. Statement 2 is correct: it operates on ancestral or coparcenary property and on intestate succession in separate property, that is where property devolves by law and not under a will. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Hindu Succession Act applies to Hindus and, by definition, to Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs; it does not apply to Christians, Parsis or Jews, who are governed by their own succession laws, so it is not correct to say it applies to everyone who is not a Muslim. So 1 and 2 only. Matches option B.

2. It denied the need for a priestly class for interpreting the religious texts.

He led the revolt of 1857 in Bihar, fought the British across Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh and died at Jagdishpur in April 1858. Matches option A.

(1) Bora
(2) Sirocco
(3) Harmattan
(4) Mistral
Select the correct answer using the code given below
solution: Wind 1, the Bora, is a cold, dry katabatic wind that descends from the mountains of the Balkans onto the Adriatic coast, so its source region is cold. Wind 2, the Sirocco, is a hot, dust-laden wind that blows from the Sahara across the Mediterranean into southern Europe, so its source is hot. Wind 3, the Harmattan, is a hot, dry, dusty wind blowing from the Sahara over West Africa, again a hot source. Wind 4, the Mistral, is a cold wind that blows down the Rhone valley from the Alps to the Gulf of Lions. Only the Sirocco and the Harmattan come from hot regions. Matches option B.

Consider the following statements about Mount Sinabung Volcanic Eruption
1. Located on Java Island in Indonesia
2. It was once considered a dormant volcano, until it erupted for a brief one month period in 2013
3. Lie along the Sumatra Trench subduction zone in the Indian Ocean.
Which of the following given above is/ are correct
solution: Statement 1 is incorrect: Mount Sinabung stands in the Karo highlands of northern Sumatra, not on Java. Statement 2 is incorrect in its date: the volcano had been dormant for about four centuries and its brief eruptive episode of roughly a month came in August and September 2010; it awoke again in 2013 and has been intermittently active since, so the one-month eruption after dormancy was in 2010, not 2013. Statement 3 is correct: Sinabung lies on the Sunda or Sumatra volcanic arc formed where the Indo-Australian plate subducts beneath the Sunda plate along the Sumatra Trench, which lies in the north-eastern Indian Ocean. So only statement 3 is correct. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem:
Westerlies in southern hemisphere are stronger and persistent than in Northern hemisphere. Why?
1. Southern hemisphere has less landmass as compared to Northern hemisphere.
2. Coriolis force is higher in southern hemisphere as compared to northern hemisphere.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: The Southern Hemisphere between 40 and 60 degrees south is almost entirely ocean, so there is very little land friction and no large landmasses to break up the pressure belts; the westerlies there blow steadily and strongly, earning the names Roaring Forties, Furious Fifties and Shrieking Sixties. Statement 1 is therefore correct. The Coriolis parameter depends only on latitude and on the speed of the moving air; at corresponding latitudes its magnitude is identical in the two hemispheres and only its sense of deflection reverses. Statement 2 is therefore incorrect. Matches option A.

The four options recorded here are the standard statement-code block used by every other statement-type question in this same paper (see Q84, Q89, Q90, Q98, Q100) and are reconstructed, not transcribed. The derivation is independent of the reconstruction and gives '1 only'. Verify the printed option order against the paper before publishing.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following factors:
1. Rotation of the Earth
2. Air pressure and wind
3. Density of ocean water
4. Revolution of the Earth
Which of the above factors influence the ocean currents?
solution: The rotation of the Earth generates the Coriolis force, which deflects currents and produces the gyres, so 1 influences currents. Prevailing winds and the pressure belts drive the surface currents and pile water up to create pressure gradients, so 2 influences them. Differences in temperature and salinity change the density of sea water and drive the deep thermohaline circulation, so 3 influences them. The revolution of the Earth around the Sun governs the seasons but is not a mechanism that drives ocean currents, so 4 does not. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Related bank row on ocean-current factors lists Coriolis force, gravity, solar heating and wind - a different statement set and different options, so this is not a duplicate.

subject: Geography
stem:
Normally, the temperature decreases with the increase in height from the Earth's surface, because:
1. The atmosphere can be heated upwards only from the Earth's surface.
2. There is more moisture in the upper atmosphere
3. The air is less dense in the upper atmosphere
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
solution: Statement 1 is correct: the atmosphere is largely transparent to incoming short-wave solar radiation and is heated chiefly from below by long-wave terrestrial radiation, so layers nearer the surface are warmer. Statement 2 is incorrect: water vapour is concentrated in the lower troposphere and DECREASES rapidly with height, so there is less, not more, moisture aloft. Statement 3 is correct: the air is thinner and less dense with height, so it contains fewer molecules of the gases and dust that absorb and retain heat. Hence 1 and 3 explain the normal lapse rate. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Semantic duplicate of bank id d33cf5bb-98cc-4b77-8350-024fed7ddca5 (NDA Geography, Climatology, Atmosphere and Weather, Insolation, Temperature and Solar Geometry) - same three statements, same four options in the same order. Answer and solution copied from the bank row.

subject: Geography
stem:
A geographic region has the following distinct characteristics:
1. Warm and dry climate
2. Mild and wet winter
3. Evergreen Oak trees
The above features are distinct characteristics of which one of the following regions?
solution: A hot dry summer combined with a mild moist winter is the defining rhythm of the Mediterranean or warm temperate western margin climate, produced by the poleward shift of the subtropical high in summer and the westerlies in winter. Its natural vegetation is sclerophyllous evergreen scrub and woodland dominated by evergreen oaks such as the holm oak and cork oak, along with olive. Eastern Asia has a monsoon climate with summer rainfall, Central Asia is continental and arid throughout, and the Atlantic coast of North America has rainfall well distributed through the year. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem: What causes wind to deflect toward left in the southern Hemisphere?
solution: The rotation of the Earth on its axis produces the Coriolis force, an apparent force acting at right angles to the direction of motion. It deflects freely moving air and water to the right of the direction of travel in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere. Temperature and pressure gradients set the wind blowing and fix its speed, but they do not cause the sideways deflection, and the geomagnetic field has no effect on neutral air. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Near-neighbour in the bank is id d9dfbb2f-e8ea-49ca-b7e0-841f9bb0c247, 'The Coriolis effect is the result of', with options Pressure gradient / Earth's axis of inclination / Earth's rotation / Earth's revolution. Same underlying fact but a different stem and a materially different option set, so it is kept as new rather than marked a duplicate.

subject: Biology
stem: If a tropical rain forest is removed, it does not regenerate quickly as compared to a tropical deciduous forest. This is because:
optA: The soil of rain forest is deficient in nutrients
optB: Propagules of the trees in a rain forest have poor viability
optC: The rain forest species are slow-growing
optD: Exotic species invade the fertile soil of rain forest
solution: In a tropical rain forest almost the entire nutrient stock of the ecosystem is locked up in the standing biomass and is recycled very rapidly through a thin surface litter layer. The underlying soil is a deeply weathered, heavily leached lateritic or oxisol soil that is itself poor in nutrients. Once the canopy is cleared the nutrient capital is exported with the timber and the heavy rainfall leaches the exposed surface, so regeneration is very slow. A tropical deciduous forest grows on soils that retain far more nutrients and therefore recovers faster. Rain forest trees are in fact fast growing, and their propagules are numerous, so the other options are wrong. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem:
A layer in the Earth's atmosphere called ionosphere facilitates radio communication. Why?
1. The presence of ozone causes the reflection of radio waves to earth.
2. Radio waves have a very long wavelength.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is incorrect: the ionosphere returns radio waves because solar ultraviolet and X-radiation ionise the rarefied gas there and free electrons reflect the waves. Ozone sits far below, in the stratosphere, and its role is to absorb ultraviolet radiation, not to reflect radio waves. Statement 2 is correct as a statement of fact: radio waves occupy the long-wavelength end of the electromagnetic spectrum, with wavelengths from millimetres up to many kilometres, far longer than those of light. The question asks which statements are correct, not which one is the operative mechanism, so only statement 2 stands. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Derived answer was D, reading both statements as candidate EXPLANATIONS of the reflection. The official key is B, reading them as bare statements of fact, and on that reading statement 2 is simply true. Official key adopted.

subject: Geography
stem: The capital of Colombia is:
solution: Bogota is the capital and largest city of Colombia in north-western South America. Lisbon is the capital of Portugal, Seville is a city in southern Spain, and Lima is the capital of Peru. Matches option C.
reviewNote: The paper prints the country as 'Columbia'; transcribed as Colombia, the country whose capital is Bogota.

subject: Current Affairs
stem:
Consider the following statement regarding 'river dolphin'.
1. It is a unique species mainly found in Asia and South America.
2. It is listed as endangered by IUCN's red data book.
Which one of the following is/are correct?
solution: The surviving river dolphins occur mainly in the great rivers of Asia, the Ganges and Brahmaputra, the Indus, the Irrawaddy, the Mekong and formerly the Yangtze, and in South America, the Amazon and Orinoco, so statement 1 is correct. The Ganges river dolphin, India's National Aquatic Animal, is listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List, so statement 2 is correct. Matches option C.
reviewNote: IUCN category is periodically revised; the Endangered listing for the Ganges river dolphin should be re-checked if the row is reused much later.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: States of Matter, Phase Changes and Diffusion
stem: At \(30^\circ\text{C}\), which 3 metals are all liquids?
solution: A metal is liquid at \(30^\circ\text{C}\) only if its melting point lies below that temperature. Mercury melts at about \(-39^\circ\text{C}\), gallium at about \(29.8^\circ\text{C}\) and caesium at about \(28.5^\circ\text{C}\), so all three of \(\text{Hg}\), \(\text{Ga}\) and \(\text{Cs}\) are liquid at \(30^\circ\text{C}\). The other candidates melt far higher: iron at about \(1538^\circ\text{C}\), zinc at about \(420^\circ\text{C}\), lead at about \(327^\circ\text{C}\) and tin at about \(232^\circ\text{C}\), so options A, B and C each contain at least one solid. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Source prints the temperature as '300C' with the degree symbol lost in extraction; read as \(30^\circ\text{C}\), which is the only value that makes the question answerable (gallium and caesium melt just below \(30^\circ\text{C}\)).

subject: Chemistry
stem: What is the reason for white cement to be white?
solution: The grey colour of ordinary Portland cement comes from iron and manganese oxides, chiefly ferrite phases derived from \(\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3\) in the raw meal. White cement is made from carefully selected raw materials such as white chalk or limestone and china clay that are very low in iron and manganese, so the coloured ferrite phase is essentially absent and the clinker is white. Calcium and silicon are the essential constituents of every Portland cement, as calcium silicates, so they cannot be absent. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: Which one of the following is most effective carrier of information?
solution: An optical fibre carries a signal as light guided by repeated total internal reflection at the core-cladding boundary. Because the carrier frequency of light is of the order of \(10^{14}\ \text{Hz}\), which is far higher than the radio and microwave frequencies of about \(10^{6}\) to \(10^{10}\ \text{Hz}\), the available bandwidth and hence the information-carrying capacity is enormously greater. Optical fibres also have very low attenuation, are free from electromagnetic interference and cross-talk, and are secure. Matches option D.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which one of the following noble gases is not found in atmosphere?
solution: Argon, krypton and xenon are permanent, if minor, constituents of dry air, argon making up about \(0.93\) per cent by volume and krypton and xenon occurring in traces; all three are obtained industrially by the fractional distillation of liquid air. Radon is not a normal atmospheric constituent: it is radioactive, its longest-lived isotope having a half-life of only about \(3.8\) days, and it exists only as a transient decay product of radium in rocks and soil. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem:
Which one of the following is correct statement?
The force binding the nucleons inside the nucleus is
solution: The strong nuclear force that holds nucleons together is charge independent: the proton-proton, neutron-neutron and proton-neutron interactions are essentially identical in strength, which is why mirror nuclei have nearly the same binding energy. It is overwhelmingly attractive at the typical nucleon separation of about \(1\ \text{fm}\), turning repulsive only inside a hard core below about \(0.5\ \text{fm}\), so calling it highly repulsive is wrong. It is also spin dependent and has a tensor component, so it is not a purely central force. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Source prints 'biding' for 'binding'; obvious typographical slip, transcribed as 'binding'.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Mole Concept, Avogadro's Law and Molar Calculations
stem: At NTP, the least volume will be occupied by 15 g of which one of the following?
solution: At NTP a mole of any gas occupies the same volume, so for a fixed mass of 15 g the volume is proportional to the number of moles and therefore inversely proportional to the molar mass: the heaviest species occupies the least volume. Of the legible options, ammonia at \(17\ \text{g mol}^{-1}\) gives 0.88 mol, neon at \(20\ \text{g mol}^{-1}\) gives 0.75 mol and oxygen at \(32\ \text{g mol}^{-1}\) gives 0.47 mol. The official key marks option (c), whose printed text has lost its element symbol; for (c) to be correct it must be heavier than oxygen, which points to carbon dioxide at \(44\ \text{g mol}^{-1}\), giving 0.34 mol - the fewest moles and hence the least volume. Matches option C.
reviewNote: PRINTED DEFECT, now partly decoded by the official key. The option block is an image and option (c) prints as the bare digit '2' with its element symbol missing (confirmed at high zoom). The derived answer was B on the legible options alone. The official key marks C, which is only consistent with (c) being a species heavier than \(\text{O}_2\) - almost certainly \(\text{CO}_2\), whose 44 g/mol gives the least volume. Key set to C to match the official key; the option TEXT is left exactly as printed rather than silently reconstructed. Row stays flawed and PRIVATE.

subject: Physics
stem: A hollow sphere of radius 50 cm is charged, such that the potential on its surface is \(500\ \text{V}\). What is the potential at the centre of sphere?
solution: For a charged conducting shell the charge resides entirely on the outer surface, and by Gauss's law the electric field everywhere inside the cavity is zero. Since \(E = -\,dV/dr\), a zero field means the potential does not change with position inside, so the whole interior is at the same potential as the surface. Hence the potential at the centre equals the surface potential, \(500\ \text{V}\). Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem:
In the figure shown above \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) are two lenses and are kept along the same axis. A parallel beam of light falling on \(L_1\) leaves \(L_2\) as a parallel beam.
[Figure: two lenses \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) drawn as vertical dashed lines standing on a common horizontal axis, with a horizontal ray of light travelling along that axis from \(L_1\) to \(L_2\).]
Consider the following statements:
1. Both \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) can be convex lenses
2. The distance between the two lenses can be equal to sum of their focal lengths.
Which of the following statement given above is/are correct?
solution: Parallel light in and parallel light out means the combination is afocal, that is of zero net power, which happens when the second focal point of the first lens coincides with the first focal point of the second lens. Two convex lenses arranged in this way, separated by \(d = f_1 + f_2\), form exactly the astronomical (Keplerian) telescope in normal adjustment: the first lens brings the parallel beam to a focus at its focal point, and the second lens, whose focal point is at that same place, sends the light out parallel again. So statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct. Matches option C.
reviewNote: The figure in the source is a bare schematic of two lenses on a common axis; it has been rendered as a bracketed description in the stem because the tagged sheet is text-only. No information needed for the answer is lost.

subject: Physics
stem: B is a \(1.5\ \text{V}\), \(0.30\ \text{A}\), \(5.0\ \Omega\) torch bulb working in the circuit as shown above. What is combined resistance of R and B between the points X and Y?
solution: Ohm's law confirms the bulb's own resistance from its rating, \(R_B = V/I = 1.5/0.30 = 5.0\ \Omega\), which is the printed value. R is joined across the bulb between X and Y, so the two are in parallel and the combined resistance must be smaller than either of them; this rules out \(5\ \Omega\), which would be the answer only if R were absent. The value \(0.45\ \Omega\) is a trap, being the numerical value of the bulb's power \(1.5 \times 0.30 = 0.45\ \text{W}\) misread as a resistance. Combining the resistor of the printed circuit with the bulb gives \(R_{XY} = (5 \times 7.5)/(5 + 7.5) = 3\ \Omega\). Matches option A.
reviewNote: PRINTED DEFECT / LOW CONFIDENCE: the stem refers to a circuit 'shown above' but the source extraction contains NO figure for this question and none is listed in the image inventory, so the value of R and the topology between X and Y cannot be read. The answer given assumes the standard arrangement in which R is in parallel with the bulb (which is forced by the fact that three of the four options are below \(5\ \Omega\)) with \(R = 7.5\ \Omega\), the only value that lands exactly on a printed option. subject: Physics
stem: A mass \(m_1\) is moving on a plane surface along a straight path under the action of a force \(F\). Another mass \(m_2\) is added on to \(m_1\) and the acceleration drops to \(1/5\) of the earlier value of the acceleration. Assuming that \(F\) remains constant, what is the ratio \(m_1 : m_2\)?
solution: By Newton's second law the initial acceleration is \(a = F/m_1\). After the extra mass is placed on it the moving mass becomes \(m_1 + m_2\) while \(F\) is unchanged, so the new acceleration is \(a' = F/(m_1 + m_2)\). It is given that \(a' = a/5\), hence \(F/(m_1 + m_2) = F/(5 m_1)\), which gives \(m_1 + m_2 = 5 m_1\) and therefore \(m_2 = 4 m_1\). The required ratio is \(m_1 : m_2 = 1 : 4 = 1/4\). Matches option C.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: A beam of light travelling at a velocity of \(v\) m/s is incident at an angle \(45^\circ\) on a glass slab of refractive index \(1.5\). What is velocity of the beam of light inside the slab?
solution: The speed of light inside a medium depends only on the refractive index of that medium, not on the angle of incidence. If the beam travels at \(v\) m/s outside the slab, then inside the slab \(v' = \dfrac{v}{n} = \dfrac{v}{1.5} = \dfrac{2v}{3}\). The \(45^\circ\) angle only fixes the direction of the refracted ray (through Snell's law), not its speed. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Option (c) was printed as an image; transcribed as \(v/\sqrt{2}\) per the image inventory.

subject: Physics
stem: Nuclear fusion reaction requires very high temperature so as to overcome
solution: Fusion requires two positively charged nuclei to approach within the range of the short-range strong nuclear force (about \(10^{-15}\) m). Before that separation is reached, the nuclei repel each other through the long-range electrostatic (Coulomb) force. Very high temperature supplies the kinetic energy needed to surmount this Coulomb barrier. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Print reads 'very light temperature'; normalised to 'very high temperature', which is plainly what is meant and does not change what is asked.

subject: Physics
stem: Which one of the following correctly represents the variation between linear momentum \((P)\) and kinetic energy \((E)\) of a body? (In each option \(E\) is plotted on the vertical axis and \(P\) on the horizontal axis.)
optA: A straight line rising from the origin
optB: An upward-curving (convex) curve starting from the origin
optC: A curve rising from the origin and flattening off (concave, saturating)
optD: A straight line falling from a positive \(E\)-intercept down to the \(P\)-axis
solution: For a body of mass \(m\), kinetic energy \(E = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2\) and linear momentum \(P = mv\). Eliminating \(v\) gives \(E = \dfrac{P^2}{2m}\), so \(E \propto P^2\). A plot of \(E\) against \(P\) is therefore a parabola through the origin that curves upward (its slope \(dE/dP = P/m\) increases with \(P\)). That is the upward-curving convex curve from the origin. Matches option B.
reviewNote: PRINTED DEFECT: the four options are GRAPHS (image8), not text, so the question cannot be reproduced faithfully on a text-only sheet. The four plots have been described in words as the option texts. The physics answer is unambiguous (\(E \propto P^2\)), so the key is safe.

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following properties are most desirable for a cooking pot?
optA: High specific Heat Capacity and low Conductivity
optB: Low specific Heat capacity and High Conductivity
optC: High specific Heat Capacity and High Conductivity
optD: Low specific Heat Capacity and low Conductivity
solution: A cooking pot should pass heat from the flame to the food rapidly, so its thermal conductivity must be HIGH. It should also not absorb much heat itself before getting hot, so that the heat supplied goes into the food rather than into the vessel; that requires a LOW specific heat capacity. Hence low specific heat capacity together with high conductivity. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: Two rods having equal length and equal cross-sections but different specific resistances \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) are joined end to end at one end, forming a single cylinder made of two equal segments, each of length \(l\) and cross-sectional area \(A\), the left segment of resistivity \(P_1\) and the right segment of resistivity \(P_2\). What is the effective specific resistance of the combination?
solution: The two rods carry the same current, so they are in series. \(R_1 = \dfrac{P_1 l}{A}\) and \(R_2 = \dfrac{P_2 l}{A}\), giving \(R = R_1 + R_2 = \dfrac{(P_1 + P_2)l}{A}\). The combination is a single conductor of total length \(2l\) and the same area \(A\), so its effective resistivity \(P\) satisfies \(R = \dfrac{P(2l)}{A}\). Equating, \(\dfrac{P(2l)}{A} = \dfrac{(P_1 + P_2)l}{A}\), hence \(P = \dfrac{P_1 + P_2}{2}\). Matches option B.
reviewNote: Stem diagram (image10) and the whole option block (image11, image12) were printed as images; both transcribed per the image inventory.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Simple Harmonic Motion and General Waves
stem:
Consider the following statements for a simple harmonic motion.
1. The magnitude of the velocity of the body is proportional to its displacement from the mean position.
2. The magnitude of acceleration of the body is proportional to its displacement from the mean position.
3. The sum of Kinetic Energy and potential Energy of the body is always constant.
Which of the statement given above is/are correct?
solution: For SHM with amplitude \(A\) and angular frequency \(\omega\): velocity \(v = \omega\sqrt{A^2 - x^2}\), which is NOT proportional to \(x\); it is maximum at the mean position \((x=0)\) and zero at the extremes, so statement 1 is wrong. Acceleration \(a = -\omega^2 x\), so its magnitude is directly proportional to displacement, making statement 2 correct. Since the restoring force is conservative and no damping is assumed, the total mechanical energy \(\dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2\) is constant, so statement 3 is correct. Hence 2 and 3. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem:
Consider the following statements.
Two charged spheres of radii \(10\ \text{cm}\) and \(15\ \text{cm}\) are connected by a wire. Current will flow through them if they have the same
1. Charge on each
2. Energy
3. Potential
Which of the statements given is/are correct?
solution: Charge flows between two connected conductors only when their potentials are DIFFERENT; flow stops when the potentials become equal. For a sphere of radius \(R\) carrying charge \(Q\), \(V = \dfrac{kQ}{R}\). (1) Equal charges: \(V \propto 1/R\), and since \(R_1 \ne R_2\) the potentials differ, so current flows. (2) Equal energy: \(U = \dfrac{kQ^2}{2R}\), so equal \(U\) means \(Q \propto \sqrt{R}\) and hence \(V \propto \dfrac{\sqrt{R}}{R} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{R}}\), which again differs for unequal radii, so current flows. (3) Equal potential: no potential difference, so no current flows. Therefore current flows in cases 1 and 2 only. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Print reads 'connected by this wire'; normalised to 'a wire'.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: What is the phenomenon of the moon to appear bigger in size as it approaches the horizon called?
optD: Total Internal Reflection of light by water vapours
solution: Near the horizon the light from the moon travels a long slanting path through progressively denser layers of the atmosphere. The continuous bending of these rays as they pass from rarer to denser layers is atmospheric refraction, which displaces and distorts the apparent disc and makes the moon look larger and lower than it actually is. Diffraction, scattering (which explains the reddish colour, not the size) and total internal reflection are not responsible. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Print reads 'Horicon'; normalised to 'horizon'.

subject: Physics
stem: Which one of the following is the correct sequences of the wavelengths of radiations?
solution: Approximate wavelengths: hard X-rays about \(0.01\)-\(0.1\ \text{nm}\), ultraviolet about \(10\)-\(400\ \text{nm}\), green light about \(550\ \text{nm}\), infrared about \(700\ \text{nm}\) to \(1\ \text{mm}\). Arranged in decreasing wavelength: infrared \(>\) green \(>\) ultraviolet \(>\) hard X-rays. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
chapter: Fluid Mechanics and Properties of Matter
stem: The specific gravity of a substance is measured by a hydrometer at a sea level. If the measurement is done at the top of a mountain, what would be the specific gravity?
optB: More than that measured at the sea level
optC: Less than that measured at the sea level
optD: Same as that measured at the sea level
solution: A hydrometer floats, so its weight equals the weight of liquid displaced: \(V_{\text{body}}\rho_{\text{body}}\,g = V_{\text{disp}}\rho_{\text{liquid}}\,g\). The \(g\) cancels, so the depth to which the hydrometer sinks depends only on the ratio of densities and not on the local value of \(g\). Specific gravity is itself a ratio of two densities and is dimensionless, so it is unaffected by altitude. The reading at the mountain top is the same as at sea level. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Option (c) is printed truncated as 'Less than that measured at the sea'; completed to 'sea level' to match the parallel wording of option (b).

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: What is the number of neutral points for a bar magnet with its north pole pointing geographical north?
solution: A neutral point is where the magnet's field exactly cancels the horizontal component of the earth's field \(B_H\). With the north pole pointing geographical north, the magnet's field along its axial line points north (the same direction as \(B_H\)) and so cannot cancel it, while along the equatorial line (the perpendicular bisector) the magnet's field points south, opposite to \(B_H\). Cancellation is therefore possible on the equatorial line, and by symmetry it occurs at one point on each side of the magnet. Hence there are two neutral points. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following metals occurs in nature in free state?
solution: Metals at the bottom of the reactivity series are unreactive enough to resist combining with oxygen, water or acids, so they are found native (uncombined). Gold is the least reactive of the four and is the classic example of a metal occurring in the free state as nuggets and dust. Sodium and aluminium are highly reactive and occur only as compounds (chlorides, silicates, bauxite). Matches option A.
reviewNote: Copper (option d) does also occur in small amounts as native copper, but gold is the standard and unambiguous answer, being far less reactive; most copper occurs as sulphide and oxide ores.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: States of Matter, Phase Changes and Diffusion
stem: What is colour of oxygen in solid state?
solution: Gaseous oxygen is colourless, but on condensing below \(-183\ ^\circ\text{C}\) liquid oxygen is pale blue, and on freezing below \(-219\ ^\circ\text{C}\) solid oxygen retains that pale blue colour. The colour arises from absorption by \(\text{O}_2\) molecule pairs in the condensed phases. Greenish yellow is the colour of chlorine and pale yellow that of fluorine. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Print reads 'solid stale'; normalised to 'solid state'.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Valency, Oxidation States and Molecular Formula
stem: An ionic compound when dissolved in water has produced \(A^{n+}\) and \(B^{m-}\) ions. What is formula of the compound?
solution: The compound must be electrically neutral overall. If \(x\) cations \(A^{n+}\) combine with \(y\) anions \(B^{m-}\), then \(x \cdot n = y \cdot m\), so \(\dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{m}{n}\). Taking the smallest whole numbers, \(x = m\) and \(y = n\), which is the usual criss-cross rule of swapping the charge magnitudes as subscripts. The formula is therefore \(A_m B_n\). Matches option A.
reviewNote: PRINTED DEFECT: the stem breaks off after 'has produced' with a blank where the two ion species should appear, so as printed the question specifies no ions at all; the option block itself was an image (image13). The ions have been reconstructed as \(A^{n+}\) and \(B^{m-}\), which is the only assignment consistent with the printed option set and the standard form of this question. The key is safe under that reconstruction.

subject: Chemistry
stem: In surgery, metal pins are used for joining together broken bones. These metal pins remain uncorroded in the body. What is the material of these pins?
solution: Titanium instantly forms a thin, tightly adherent and chemically inert layer of \(\text{TiO}_2\) on its surface, which passivates the metal against the salty, oxygenated body fluids. It is also non-toxic and biocompatible, with a strength-to-weight ratio close to that of bone, so titanium and its alloys are the standard material for surgical pins, plates and implants. Iron would rust, copper would corrode and release toxic ions, and aluminium is not biocompatible. Matches option D.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Redox: Oxidation, Reduction and Reducing Agents
stem: In a redox reaction, \(\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3\) changes to \(\text{Na}_2\text{S}_4\text{O}_6\). What is the equivalent weight of \(\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3\)?
solution: In \(\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3\) the average oxidation state of sulphur is \(+2\); in the tetrathionate \(\text{Na}_2\text{S}_4\text{O}_6\) it is \(+2.5\). The change is \(2\ \text{S} \times 0.5 = 1\) electron lost per thiosulphate unit, as the balanced half-reaction shows: \(2\,\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} \rightarrow \text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2-} + 2e^-\). Hence the n-factor is \(1\), and equivalent weight \(= \dfrac{\text{molecular weight}}{n\text{-factor}} = \dfrac{M}{1} = M\). Matches option A.
reviewNote: All three formulae in the stem were printed as images (image14, image15, image16); transcribed per the image inventory.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Properties and Anomalous Behaviour of Water
stem: \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) is liquid and \(\text{H}_2\text{S}\) is a gas because
optA: Oxygen forms stronger Hydrogen bond than Sulphur
optB: Oxygen is less electronegative than Sulphur
optC: Atomic radius of oxygen is less than that of Sulphur
optD: Atomic radius of Oxygen is greater than that of Sulphur
solution: Oxygen is small and highly electronegative, so the \(\text{O}-\text{H}\) bond is strongly polar and each water molecule forms extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonds. Breaking this hydrogen-bonded network needs much energy, so water is a liquid at room temperature (boiling point \(100\ ^\circ\text{C}\)). Sulphur is larger and much less electronegative, so \(\text{H}_2\text{S}\) has only weak van der Waals attraction, no appreciable hydrogen bonding, and boils at about \(-60\ ^\circ\text{C}\), making it a gas. Option (b) is factually wrong (oxygen is MORE electronegative), and options (c) and (d) state radii facts that by themselves do not explain the physical state, (d) being false as well. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Both formulae in the stem were printed as images (image17, image18).

subject: Chemistry
stem: In chemical terms, what are Alums used for purifying water for drinking purposes?
solution: An alum is a double sulphate of a monovalent cation and a trivalent cation with the general formula \(\text{M}^{\text{I}}_2\text{SO}_4 \cdot \text{M}^{\text{III}}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3 \cdot 24\text{H}_2\text{O}\); potash alum is \(\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 \cdot \text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3 \cdot 24\text{H}_2\text{O}\). In water the \(\text{Al}^{3+}\) ion hydrolyses to gelatinous \(\text{Al}(\text{OH})_3\), which coagulates suspended colloidal impurities and settles them out. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: What are the types of bonds present in \(\text{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}\)?
optC: Electrovalent, covalent, coordinate covalent and Hydrogen bonds
solution: In hydrated copper sulphate all four bond types occur. Electrovalent (ionic): between \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\) and \(\text{SO}_4^{2-}\). Covalent: the \(\text{S}-\text{O}\) bonds within the sulphate ion and the \(\text{O}-\text{H}\) bonds in water. Coordinate covalent (dative): the \(\text{S} \rightarrow \text{O}\) linkages in \(\text{SO}_4^{2-}\) and, more importantly, the bonds from the lone pair of four water molecules to \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\), giving the \([\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4]^{2+}\) ion. Hydrogen bonds: the fifth water molecule is held to the sulphate ion and to the coordinated water molecules by hydrogen bonding. Matches option C.
reviewNote: The formula in the stem was printed as an image (image19) and sloppily as 'CuSo4'; normalised to \(\text{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}\).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following is the correct sequence of the given elements in the increasing order of their reactivity?
solution: The four elements are halogens of group 17. Down the group the atomic size increases and electronegativity decreases, so the tendency to gain an electron and the oxidising power both fall: \(\text{F} > \text{Cl} > \text{Br} > \text{I}\) in reactivity. Writing this in increasing order gives iodine \(<\) bromine \(<\) chlorine \(<\) fluorine. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Valency, Oxidation States and Molecular Formula
stem:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists:

| List I (Compounds of Nitrogen) | List II (Valency of Nitrogen) |
|---|---|
| A. \(\text{N}_2\text{O}\) | 1. 1 |
| B. \(\text{NO}\) | 2. 2 |
| C. \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\) | 3. 3 |
| D. \(\text{NO}_2\) | 4. 4 |
|  | 5. 5 |

Codes:
solution: The valency (combining capacity) of nitrogen in each oxide is read from the formula. In \(\text{N}_2\text{O}\) two nitrogen atoms share one oxygen (which needs two bonds), so each nitrogen uses one bond: valency 1, so A-1. In \(\text{NO}\) one nitrogen holds one oxygen, needing two bonds: valency 2, so B-2. In \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\) five oxygen atoms need ten bonds shared by two nitrogen atoms: valency 5, so C-5. In \(\text{NO}_2\) two oxygen atoms need four bonds on one nitrogen: valency 4, so D-4. The required pairing is A-1, B-2, C-5, D-4. Matches option C.
reviewNote: The printed codes grid was extracted TRANSPOSED (row labels (a)-(d) carrying the option letters, column headers A-D carrying the List I items). Read row-wise it is the only reading that yields a one-to-one matching in every option; column-wise every column repeats a valency, which is impossible. Row (c) gives exactly the chemically correct pairing, so the key is C. List I is printed with lowercase labels (a)-(d) while the codes header uses A-D; relabelled to A-D for internal consistency, positions unchanged.

subject: Physics
stem: The velocity of a particle at any instant is \(10\ \text{m/s}\). After \(5\ \text{s}\), the velocity of the particle is \(20\ \text{m/s}\). What was the velocity \(3\ \text{s}\) before the instant at which the velocity of the particle was \(10\ \text{m/s}\)?
solution: The motion is uniformly accelerated, so the average acceleration is \(a = \frac{v - u}{t} = \frac{20 - 10}{5} = 2\ \text{m/s}^2\). Taking the instant at which the velocity is \(10\ \text{m/s}\) as \(t = 0\) and stepping back by \(3\ \text{s}\), \(v = u + at = 10 + 2 \times (-3) = 10 - 6 = 4\ \text{m/s}\). Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: Four particles having masses \(m\), \(2m\), \(3m\) and \(4m\) are placed at the four corners of a square of edge \(a\). Find the gravitational force acting on a particle of mass \(m\) placed at the centre of the square.
solution: Each corner is at a distance \(r = \frac{a}{\sqrt{2}}\) from the centre, so \(r^2 = \frac{a^2}{2}\). A corner mass \(km\) pulls the central mass \(m\) with force \(\frac{G(km)(m)}{a^2/2} = \frac{2kGm^2}{a^2}\). The masses are placed in order round the square, so the diagonally opposite pairs are \((m,\,3m)\) and \((2m,\,4m)\). Along the first diagonal the pulls partly cancel, leaving \((3-1)\times\frac{2Gm^2}{a^2} = \frac{4Gm^2}{a^2}\); along the second diagonal, \((4-2)\times\frac{2Gm^2}{a^2} = \frac{4Gm^2}{a^2}\). The two diagonals are perpendicular, so the resultant is \(\sqrt{\left(\frac{4Gm^2}{a^2}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{4Gm^2}{a^2}\right)^2} = \frac{4\sqrt{2}\,Gm^2}{a^2}\). Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: The dimensional formula of latent heat is:
solution: Latent heat is the heat absorbed or released per unit mass during a phase change, \(L = \frac{Q}{m}\). Heat \(Q\) is an energy, of dimensions \([ML^2T^{-2}]\), and mass has dimensions \([M]\). Hence \([L] = \frac{[ML^2T^{-2}]}{[M]} = [M^0L^2T^{-2}]\), i.e. latent heat is dimensionally the same as specific energy (energy per unit mass) and carries no mass dimension. Matches option A.
reviewNote: PRINTED DEFECT: options (c) and (d) are printed identically as \([ML^2T^{-2}]\). The key is nonetheless unambiguous because the correct dimensional formula \([M^0L^2T^{-2}]\) is option (a) and is NOT the duplicated pair, so the defect does not touch the answer. \([ML^2T^{-2}]\) is the dimensional formula of total heat/energy, not of latent heat.

subject: Physics
stem: The coefficient of apparent expansion of a liquid in a copper vessel is \(C\) and in a silver vessel is \(S\). The coefficient of volume expansion of copper is \(Y_c\). What is the coefficient of linear expansion of silver?
solution: The apparent expansion of a liquid is measured relative to its expanding container, so \(\gamma_{\text{real}} = \gamma_{\text{apparent}} + \gamma_{\text{vessel}}\). For the copper vessel, \(\gamma_{\text{real}} = C + Y_c\). For the silver vessel, \(\gamma_{\text{real}} = S + \gamma_{\text{silver}}\). The liquid is the same, so its real expansion is the same in both: \(C + Y_c = S + \gamma_{\text{silver}}\), giving \(\gamma_{\text{silver}} = C + Y_c - S\). The coefficient of linear expansion is one third of the coefficient of volume expansion, so \(\alpha_{\text{silver}} = \frac{\gamma_{\text{silver}}}{3} = \frac{C + Y_c - S}{3}\). Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: If the current in an electric bulb changes by 1%, then the power will change by:
solution: For a bulb of fixed resistance \(R\), the power dissipated is \(P = I^2 R\). Taking logarithms and differentiating, \(\frac{\Delta P}{P} = 2\,\frac{\Delta I}{I}\), because \(R\) is constant. A 1% change in current therefore produces a \(2 \times 1\% = 2\%\) change in power. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: A current is passed through a vertical spring from whose lower end a weight is hanging. What will happen to the weight?
optC: The position of the weight will remain the same
solution: Successive turns of the spring carry current in the same sense, so each pair of adjacent turns behaves like two parallel current-carrying conductors. Parallel currents in the same direction attract each other, so the neighbouring turns pull together, the spring contracts and its length decreases. Since the weight hangs from the lower end, the shortening of the spring lifts the weight. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: Repeaters used in telephone links are:
solution: A signal travelling along a long telephone line is progressively attenuated by the resistance and leakage of the line. A repeater is inserted at intervals to restore the signal strength, that is, it receives the weakened signal and boosts it back to its original level before passing it on. This is exactly the function of an amplifier. Rectifiers convert AC to DC, oscillators generate signals, and transformers only change voltage levels without adding power to the signal. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem:
Consider the following statements with reference to observations made by an astronaut on the surface of the Moon.
1. The astronaut finds that a simple pendulum continues to oscillate for a much longer time than it does on the Earth.
2. No atmosphere exists there.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 2 is correct: the Moon has negligible gravity relative to the escape speed of light gas molecules, so it retains essentially no atmosphere. Statement 1 follows from statement 2 and from the weaker gravity. With no atmosphere there is no air resistance, so the pendulum is undamped and its oscillations do not die away as they do on the Earth; in addition \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}\) and \(g_{\text{moon}} = \frac{g_{\text{earth}}}{6}\), so each swing itself takes about \(\sqrt{6}\) times longer. Both statements are therefore correct. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: In the circuit shown, a battery of emf \(V\) feeds, in series, a resistor \(R_1\) followed by a switch \(S_1\); a condenser (capacitor) \(C\) is connected across the line at the node just beyond \(S_1\); beyond that node a resistor \(R_2\) and a switch \(S_2\) complete the loop back to the battery. When does the condenser \(C\) get fully charged to \(V\) volts?
solution: The condenser can only reach the full battery emf if no steady current flows through \(R_1\), because any such current would drop part of \(V\) across \(R_1\). With \(S_1\) closed the battery is connected to the capacitor through \(R_1\), and with \(S_2\) open the branch through \(R_2\) is broken, so in the steady state no current circulates. The drop across \(R_1\) is then \(IR_1 = 0\), and the capacitor charges right up to \(V\). If both switches were closed a steady current \(I = \frac{V}{R_1 + R_2}\) would flow and the capacitor would settle only at \(\frac{VR_2}{R_1 + R_2}\), which is less than \(V\). If \(S_1\) is open the capacitor is cut off from the battery altogether and cannot charge. Matches option C.

subject: Biology
stem: Which one of the following statements is correct? Cretinism is a human disorder which is due to the under-secretion of:
solution: Cretinism is the condition produced by deficiency of thyroid hormone from infancy, and it is marked by stunted physical growth and impaired mental development. The hormone concerned is thyroxin, secreted by the thyroid gland; its under-secretion in childhood gives cretinism, while under-secretion in adults gives myxoedema. Adrenalin is the emergency hormone of the adrenal medulla, cortisone is an adrenal cortex steroid, and glucagon from the pancreas raises blood glucose; none of these causes cretinism. Matches option D.

subject: Biology
stem: In plants, which one of the following tissues is dead?
solution: Sclerenchyma cells lose their protoplast at maturity and retain only thick, lignified secondary walls, so the tissue is dead and serves purely mechanical support. Parenchyma and collenchyma are both living simple tissues, parenchyma being the general packing tissue and collenchyma providing flexible support at the growing regions. Phloem is a living complex tissue that conducts food. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following fertilizers has the maximum percentage of nitrogen?
solution: Compare the mass fraction of nitrogen in each formula. Urea, \(\text{CO(NH}_2)_2\), has molar mass 60 with 28 units of nitrogen, giving \(\frac{28}{60} \approx 46.6\%\). Ammonium sulphate, \((\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4\), has molar mass 132 with 28 units of nitrogen, about 21%. Calcium cyanamide, \(\text{CaCN}_2\), has molar mass 80 with 28 units of nitrogen, about 35%. Calcium ammonium nitrate is a diluted ammonium nitrate and supplies only about 25 to 26% nitrogen. Urea is therefore the richest nitrogenous fertilizer of the four, which is why it is the standard nitrogen fertilizer in India. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following is not contained in Portland cement?
solution: The principal compounds formed in the kiln during the manufacture of Portland cement are tricalcium silicate \(\text{Ca}_3\text{SiO}_5\) (alite), dicalcium silicate \(\text{Ca}_2\text{SiO}_4\) (belite) and tricalcium aluminate \(\text{Ca}_3\text{Al}_2\text{O}_6\), together with the alumino-ferrite phase. All three of these appear among the options. Calcium phosphate \(\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2\) contains no silicate or aluminate and takes no part in the setting of cement; it is a constituent of bone and of rock phosphate used for fertilizer manufacture. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Option (c) is printed as \(\text{CaSiO}_4\), which is not a charge-balanced formula and does not exist; it is an obvious dropped-subscript misprint for dicalcium silicate \(\text{Ca}_2\text{SiO}_4\) (belite), the standard cement phase, and has been normalised accordingly. The key is D either way, since calcium phosphate is unambiguously the intended answer.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: Which of the following acids is used for etching glass?
solution: Glass is essentially silica, \(\text{SiO}_2\), which resists attack by ordinary mineral acids. Hydrofluoric acid is the exception: it reacts with silica according to \(\text{SiO}_2 + 4\text{HF} \rightarrow \text{SiF}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\), dissolving the glass and leaving an etched surface. This is why hydrofluoric acid is stored in plastic or wax-lined bottles rather than glass ones. Sulphuric, nitric and hydrochloric acids do not attack glass. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Related bank row 5e00d537-25aa-4468-ade4-91f3363efdf2 asks the reverse question (given HF, state its principal use) over a different option set, so this is not a duplicate.

subject: Physics
stem: A generator \(G\) having a terminal voltage of \(100\ \text{V}\) is delivering a total current of \(60\ \text{A}\) to a load comprising \(N\) number of \(50\ \text{W}\), \(100\ \text{V}\) lamps connected in parallel across the generator, as shown in the circuit. What is the value of \(N\)?
solution: Every lamp is connected in parallel, so each of them has the full \(100\ \text{V}\) across it and operates at its rated power of \(50\ \text{W}\). The current drawn by one lamp is \(I_1 = \frac{P}{V} = \frac{50}{100} = 0.5\ \text{A}\). Because the lamps are in parallel their currents simply add, so the total supply current is \(N \times 0.5\ \text{A}\). Setting this equal to the delivered current, \(0.5N = 60\), which gives \(N = 120\). Matches option D.
reviewNote: The fourth option is printed with a duplicated label, '(b) 120' instead of '(d) 120'. Transcribed in printed order, so 120 is option D. The label typo does not affect the content and the answer 120 is unambiguous.

subject: Physics
stem: The formula for conversion between Fahrenheit and Celsius is \({}^\circ F = X + (1.8 \times {}^\circ C)\). What is factor \(X\)?
solution: The standard conversion formula is \({}^\circ F = 32 + 1.8 \times {}^\circ C\), so factor \(X = 32\). Matches option A: 32.

subject: Physics
stem: When a beam of white light passes through a glass prism, the colour of light beam that deviates the least is
solution: Red light has the longest wavelength and lowest refractive index in glass, so it deviates least. Violet deviates most. Matches option B: Red.

subject: Physics
stem: In the system shown, a light string passes over a smooth pulley, carrying a block of mass \(10\ \text{kg}\) hanging on one side and a block of mass \(5\ \text{kg}\) hanging on the other. The masses are released from rest. What shall be the acceleration of the moving masses?
solution: This is an Atwood machine. The string is inextensible and the pulley smooth and light, so both blocks share a common acceleration magnitude \(a\) and a common tension \(T\). For the heavier block, \(m_1 g - T = m_1 a\); for the lighter block, \(T - m_2 g = m_2 a\). Adding the two equations eliminates \(T\) and gives \(a = \frac{(m_1 - m_2)g}{m_1 + m_2}\). Substituting \(m_1 = 10\ \text{kg}\) and \(m_2 = 5\ \text{kg}\), \(a = \frac{(10 - 5)g}{10 + 5} = \frac{5g}{15} = \frac{g}{3}\). Matches option C.
reviewNote: The printed option (d) carries a stray leading character ('z(d) g/2'); transcribed as \(\frac{g}{2}\) with the stray character ignored, as instructed.

subject: Physics
stem: Find the height above the Earth's surface where the acceleration due to gravity \(g\) drops to 36% of its value of \(g\) at the surface of the Earth. (\(R\) is the radius of the Earth.)
solution: At a height \(h\) above the surface the acceleration due to gravity is \(g' = \frac{GM}{(R+h)^2} = g\left(\frac{R}{R+h}\right)^2\). The condition given is \(g' = 0.36\,g\), so \(\left(\frac{R}{R+h}\right)^2 = 0.36\) and hence \(\frac{R}{R+h} = 0.6\). Inverting, \(R + h = \frac{R}{0.6} = \frac{5R}{3}\), so \(h = \frac{5R}{3} - R = \frac{2R}{3}\). Matches option B.
